executive_summary: The Docker environment hosting the ICS lab has multiple critical and high-risk misconfigurations that could allow attackers to reach the PLC and physical process. The most dangerous path involves the simulation container's Docker socket bind mount (E8), which grants full host control and direct access to the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net). The PLC container (188415e2db7e) has CAP_NET_ADMIN and runs as root, creating a direct attack surface. The router (37c1334f848d) and EWS (dc986d347ecc) containers also have elevated network capabilities and default credentials. Attackers could exploit these to manipulate network configurations, pivot between zones, or deploy malicious containers directly on the ICS network. All findings are based on container configurations and network topology; image vulnerability scans were not performed in this assessment.

findings.title: Network capabilities added
findings.explanation: CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_NET_RAW allow full network configuration and raw socket access. An attacker could use these to bypass firewall rules or inject malicious traffic into the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC operates.

findings.title: Root user execution
findings.explanation: Running as root increases risk of container escape or privilege escalation. Combined with network capabilities, this could allow an attacker to manipulate the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC is connected.

findings.title: Writable /etc/firewall mount
findings.explanation: A writable mount to /etc/firewall allows modification of firewall rules. If compromised, this could disable protections between the admin network (grficsv3_a-grfics-admin) and the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC resides.

findings.title: Non-read-only root filesystem
findings.explanation: A writable root filesystem increases attack surface. An attacker could install persistence mechanisms or modify container binaries to target the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC is located.

findings.title: Privileged network capabilities
findings.explanation: CAP_NET_ADMIN allows full network configuration. If compromised, this could enable an attacker to modify routing/firewall rules on the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC operates.

findings.title: Root user execution
findings.explanation: Running as root increases risk of container escape. Combined with ICS network access (grficsv3_b-ics-net), this could allow direct manipulation of the PLC's network environment.

findings.title: Non-read-only root filesystem
findings.explanation: Writable root filesystem allows persistence mechanisms. If an attacker compromises this container, they could modify binaries to attack the PLC on grficsv3_b-ics-net.

findings.title: Default VNC password in environment
findings.explanation: Default credentials reduce attack surface. An attacker could brute-force or guess this password to gain access to the ICS network via the exposed VNC service on port 6080.

findings.title: Privileged network capabilities
findings.explanation: CAP_NET_ADMIN allows full network configuration. If compromised, this could enable an attacker to manipulate network settings on the DMZ network (grficsv3_c-dmz-net) which connects to the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC operates.

findings.title: Root user execution
findings.explanation: Running as root increases risk of privilege escalation. Combined with DMZ network access (grficsv3_c-dmz-net), this could allow an attacker to pivot to the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC is located.

findings.title: Writable /var/lib/mysql mount
findings.explanation: A writable mount to /var/lib/mysql could allow database tampering. If compromised, this might affect SCADA operations on the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC is connected.

findings.title: Default credentials in environment
findings.explanation: Default credentials reduce attack surface. An attacker could exploit these to gain access to the HMI application, which connects to the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC operates.

findings.title: Root user execution
findings.explanation: Running as root increases risk of privilege escalation. If compromised, this could allow access to the admin network (grficsv3_a-grfics-admin) which connects to the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC operates.

findings.title: Published web server port on DMZ
findings.explanation: Port 8888/tcp is exposed on the DMZ network (grficsv3_c-dmz-net). A web server vulnerability here could provide an entry point to the admin network (grficsv3_a-grfics-admin) which is connected to the ICS network where the PLC resides.

findings.title: Writable /docker_persistent mount
findings.explanation: A writable mount to /docker_persistent could allow persistent access to PLC configuration files. If compromised, this might enable long-term manipulation of the physical process through the PLC.

findings.title: Docker socket bind mount
findings.explanation: A bind mount to the Docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock) grants full control over the Docker host. This would allow an attacker to create/modify containers directly on the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC operates, bypassing all container isolation.

findings.title: Docker socket bind mount on ICS network
findings.explanation: A bind mount to the Docker socket grants full control over the Docker host. This would allow an attacker to create/modify containers directly on the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) where the PLC operates, bypassing all container isolation.

findings.title: ICS network containers with network capabilities
findings.explanation: Multiple containers on the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) have CAP_NET_ADMIN. This allows network configuration changes that could disrupt or manipulate PLC communications with the physical process.

findings.title: Admin network to ICS network bridging
findings.explanation: The admin network (grficsv3_a-grfics-admin) is directly connected to the ICS network (grficsv3_b-ics-net) through multiple containers. This creates multiple potential pivots to the PLC and physical process.

findings.title: Default credentials in exposed services
findings.explanation: Default credentials in exposed VNC services (EWS container) could allow unauthorized access to the admin network, which connects to the ICS network where the PLC operates.

limitations: No evidence of container escape mitigations (seccomp/AppArmor) was checked
